svg.title: Restricted coefficient convergence and the framed quotient
svg.desc: The genuine restricted tensor functor uses the completed lisse target. Finite coefficient windows and their coherent limits prove DG convergence. Full generator-module Amitsur descent gives faithfully flat descent, and the regular Hopf fibre gives the actual affine H-frame torsor and quotient of prestacks. This is not a representability theorem for the framed prestack. Solved examples retain a negative derived tensor class, test original-field monodromy after a flat cover, and display a degree-two frame homotopy.
svg.text: Restricted coefficient convergence and the framed quotient
Every smooth projective complex curve; every connected reductive H; full DG coefficients.
1. The genuine complete coefficient target — RSP.1–RSP.5
Z^restr(A) = right t-exact continuous tensor functors Rep(H) → Mod_A(Q_X).
A_r = τ^(≥−r)A; a window [−r,0] uses A_r, including all action homotopies.
M ↦ τ^(≥−r)(A_r ⊗ᴸ_A M): derived extension AND intelligent truncation.
For scalar recovery at A_n, choose r ≥ n first, then let r grow.
Z^restr(A) ≃ lim_n Z^restr(A_n), with every coherent tensor map retained.
2. Descent of the entire target — RSP.6–RSP.8
Q_X ≃ Mod_D; Mod_A(Q_X) ≃ Mod_(A⊗D), using actual compact generators.
Test the full Amitsur comparison objectwise on D, then descend all D-action maps.
First bounded-below complexes; then compatible Postnikov limits and all mapping spaces.
Flat extension is exact and conservative; no arbitrary tensor–product-limit swap is used.
3. Actual frames and the full quotient of prestacks — RSP.9–RSP.11
Y^restr ×_(Z^restr) Spec A
Fr_H(P_(z,x))
The right-hand side is the actual affine smooth H-torsor, on every DG base.
Z^restr ≃ [Y^restr / H]_fpqc; the entire action nerve and every higher path descend.
For bounded A, dualizable finite-representation values lie in the finite-lisse ind-target.
This does not assert that Y^restr is affine or ind-affine.
4. A window is not the whole derived module category — RSP.14–RSP.16
A = C[z], |z| = −2; Q = A ⊕ Aθ, |θ| = −3, dθ = z resolves C.
C ⊗ᴸ_A C = C ⊕ Cθ: the negative class has degree −3.
Its [−1,0] truncation is C. Meanwhile RHom_A(C,C) has a degree +3 class.
That map lands in C[3], outside the window. Both degree directions are retained.
5. Original coefficients and a higher frame path — RSP.12–RSP.13, RSP.17–RSP.19
C[s,s⁻¹] → C[t,t⁻¹], s ↦ t² is faithfully flat, free on {1,t}.
Monodromy t² still has independent powers over C; closed specializations miss that failure.
For GL_2 and A = C[δ]/(δ²), |δ| = −2: π_1(frames) = 0, π_2 = Mat_2(C)δ.
A second-loop frame is I_2 + Cδ du ∧ dv; each boundary edge is I_2.
Its total degree is zero; its inverse subtracts the same square-zero matrix form.
Further geometric proofs remain required
Restricted ind-affine representability and charts; the actual diagonal/localization and Hecke action;
the nilpotent Beilinson projector, support image and original-field ind-regularity;
all geometric ground fields, derived tempered and applicable microlocal/RH/ind comparisons.
